verses.text: Do not speak harshly to an older man. Instead, encourage him as you would your father. Treat younger men like brothers,
older women like mothers, and younger women like sisters, with complete purity.
Honour and care for widows who really are alone.
But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they should first learn to serve God by caring for their own family, and so pay back their parents. This pleases God.
A widow who is really alone, with no one to help her, puts her hope in God. Night and day she keeps on praying and asking God for help.
But a widow who lives just for pleasure is dead even while she is alive.
Give the people these instructions too, so that no one can find fault with them.
Anyone who does not take care of his relatives, and most of all his own family, has denied the faith. He is worse than someone who does not believe.
To be put on the list of widows, a widow must be at least sixty years old. She must have been faithful to her husband.

She must be well known for her good deeds, such as bringing up children, welcoming strangers into her home, washing the feet of God's people, helping those in trouble, and giving herself to every kind of good work.
But do not put younger widows on the list. When their own desires pull them away from Christ, they want to marry again.
Then they are judged for breaking the first promise they made.
Besides, they get into the habit of being lazy and going from house to house. And not only lazy, but they also gossip and get busy in other people's business, saying things they should not say.
So I want the younger widows to marry, to have children, and to manage their homes. Then the enemy will have no chance to speak badly of us.
Some have already turned away to follow Satan.
If any believing man or woman has widows in the family, they should help them, so that the church is not burdened. Then the church can help the widows who are really alone.
Church leaders who lead well should be counted worthy of double honour and pay, most of all those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
For the Scripture says, "Do not tie up the mouth of an ox while it is treading out the grain." And, "The worker deserves his pay."
Do not accept a charge against a church leader unless it is backed by two or three witnesses.
Correct those who keep on sinning in front of everyone, so that the others will be afraid to sin.
In front of God and Christ Jesus and the chosen angels, I command you to keep these rules without taking sides. Do nothing out of favouritism.
Do not be in a hurry to lay hands on anyone to appoint them. Do not share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
Stop drinking only water. Use a little wine for your stomach, because you are often ill.
Some people's sins are clear to see. They go ahead of them to judgment. But the sins of others only show up later.
In the same way, good deeds are clear to see. And even those that are not clear cannot stay hidden for ever.
